rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a compositional substitution (Mo replaced by W), whereas the paper's intervention is thermomechanical processing (cold rolling and annealing) of a non-equiatomic alloy. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature compression tests on a single-phase BCC alloy, while the paper uses room-temperature tensile tests on a cold-rolled and annealed alloy. The testing mode (compression vs. tension) and processing conditions differ entirely.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced electronegativity difference to lower dislocation motion resistance, while the paper's mechanism involves work hardening, dislocation tangles, texture, and subsequent recovery/recrystallization. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts enhanced plasticity with maintained compressive yield strength (~1719 MPa), whereas the paper reports changes in tensile strength and elongation due to rolling and annealing, with a different baseline alloy and property values.
